tasks.title: Route engine: set up, add ship, close, cycle-end net settlement, saturation, idle rule, stranded rescue
tasks.brief: Build the automated route engine (GDD section 2, Automated routes). Route record: unordered planet pair, ship count, level (base only), orders (empty = trade both ways). Set-up check: a free ship or buy at ship_price, room under ship_cap, both planets open, net above zero; refuse with one reason; buy and assign in one step; no setup fee. Adding a ship joins the pair's route; closing a route frees its ships at zero cost. Settle once per cycle end using the formulas in handoffs/economy-designer/2026-10-26-T10.json details.answers (1_formula, 2_saturation). Saturation is 5 credits off each leg's sell price at the selling planet per extra ship on that route, floor at buy price. A route at or below zero net idles and shows 'not profitable'. A ship's first cycle pays pro rata to the time assigned. Stranded (absorbs T46): at cycle end, if the player owns zero ships and cash is below ship_price, pay rescue_stipend (balance.json, 1000) with a notice; never end the game. Read prices from data/planets.json. Reuse game/trade.gd logic. If the cap is reached, stop and hand off partial. Handoff: handoffs/gameplay-programmer/<date>-T07.json.

tasks.title: One-way routes: buy-side and sell-side connections, auto ship assignment, stall and block rules
tasks.brief: Rework game/route_engine.gd. A route is ONE-WAY: a Buy order at planet A (planet resource -> A storage) and a Sell order at planet B (B storage -> market); a ship hauls between the two storages. Connection kinds: planet to planet now; planet to storage and storage to storage are later (space storage), keep the data model open. A planet may hold several routes while its storage allows. One ship per route, never shared. A ship is assigned automatically from the owned pool when the connection is made; if none is free, the setup says so (reason text). Rules: empty source storage -> route stalls (waits); full destination storage -> route BLOCKED: stops, emits a notification event, state red, until the player removes it, sells down the storage or sets an alternative route. Player or money missing for a buy order -> stalls. Ship limit stays (ship_cap, tune later). Purchase and maintenance stay (numbers later). REMOVE the saturation rule (5 credits off the sell price per extra ship) entirely, code and balance.json key; owner confirmed 2026-10-27. Storage fill is the only pressure. Report what you removed. Handoff: handoffs/gameplay-programmer/<date>-T56.json.

tasks.title: Local buy/sell at the planet without a route; routes only move stock; new route art
tasks.brief: Owner direction 2026-10-27. (1) The player must be able to Buy and Sell on a planet with NO route. Buy on a planet's resource row is a standing local order: each cycle it buys up to a per-cycle amount at that planet's buy price, pays cash, and adds to that planet's company storage (established on the first trade) until the storage is full or cash runs out. Sell is a standing local order that sells stock from that planet's storage at the sell price. With no outflow the storage can fill to max capacity; the order then idles with a short status (storage full), not an error. Per-cycle amount: an abstract code constant for now (use the ship load size), the economy-designer sets it later. Buy and sell each toggle on and off per commodity. No ship is needed for local orders. (2) A route is optional and only MOVES stock: a separate control on a planet's storage row ('Send to...', then click the destination planet) creates a one-way route source storage to destination storage with one auto-assigned ship; stalls when the source storage is empty, is blocked (red, notification) when the destination is full. The old 'Buy here then click the other planet and Sell' pending flow is replaced by this. Keep planet-to-storage and storage-to-storage as later options. Update the route engine, planet panel, save/load, cash forecast and the scripted checks accordingly; storage still changes only through orders and routes (no free refill). (3) New route art: assets/route/arrow_tail.png (72 px), arrow_mid.png (81 px, tile) and arrow_head.png (367 px), each 198 px tall, one whole arrow pointing right (head, diamond and fins at the destination end), transparent background. A one-way route draws ONE arrow over the full line length: tail at the source, tiled mid, head at the destination. When both directions exist on the same pair, each direction's arrow covers HALF of the line and they meet in the middle (the second one pointing the other way). Same overall thickness as the earlier art (0.18 world units per 172 px of art height); keep the straight line, the pulsing glow and the red / grey states. Remove the half-arrow ribbon code. Do not delete assets/route/half_*.png (the main session will). Handoff: handoffs/gameplay-programmer/<date>-T68.json.

tasks.title: Story: first full draft (voice, screens, events, skills, 5+ endings)
tasks.brief: First full story draft so the alpha loop reads as one coherent run from title to ending. Read only: gdd.md, gdd-skills.md, state.md, data/planets.json (names and abundant/scarce goods). No code. Write into story/ (create it): (1) voice.md: voice and glossary. Tone: serious, restrained, a small company under an indifferent sky, with occasional dry ironic humour (about one line in four, never jokes at the cost of clarity); event and ending texts carry a philosophical thread (work, enough, debt, distance, ownership, escape). Player is gender-neutral (use 'you' or 'the company'). (2) screens.md: start with a short STORY ARC (the beats from title to ending, 10 lines max), then title, preface (the player dreams of escaping society to a planet of their own, and needs money for it), menu entries, mission-board hints and tutorial lines for the first 4 cycles (click a planet, pick the resource row, Buy then Sell, one-way routes, planet storage, ship upkeep shown), key notices (route blocked, route stalled, +skill point, dead-state rescue, ship bought). Use plain UI wording from the voice file. (3) events.md: 14 to 18 events for system 1 (Voltara, Tillam, Ashgate; energy and food). Each event has an id, a title, a text of max 280 characters, and a tag copied only from this list: [price up: <planet>, <commodity>], [price down: <planet>, <commodity>], [planet closed: <planet>] (closes for a while, routes touching it are blocked). No percentages or numbers. Mix: some tell the player plainly what happens to prices, some are quiet philosophical beats with a mild effect, a few are ironic. (4) skills.md: refine the proposed skills in gdd-skills.md section 3 (A1-A5, B1-B4, C1-C4): final names, a flavour line then a plain-meaning line each (never hide an effect), max length per text. Keep ids A1..C4. You may suggest renames or one or two additions as ideas, not as changes. (5) endings.md: AT LEAST 5 endings reached by winning (cash goal reached at the end of a cycle), plus the loss ending (and a short dead-state notice, which is not an ending). The endings must differ in mood (for example: triumphant, bittersweet, quiet and peaceful, ironic or cautionary, cold or unsettling; you choose and name them). Each ending needs: id, name, mood, max 700 characters of text, and a plain condition the game can check using only things it knows: learned skill ids, count of skills per branch, the dominant branch, the cycle the cash goal was reached, final cash. Propose the selection rule as a simple table (first match wins, with one default ending so a player always gets one). Do not invent mechanics. (6) ideas.md: at most three ideas, two lines each. Every text block: stable id, max length in characters, where it appears. Run the self-check from your instructions (glossary terms, no invented numbers, no text that promises something the mechanics do not do). Handoff: handoffs/story-designer/2026-10-27-T73.json, listing which texts are ready for the gameplay-programmer to wire.
